deviations.reason: ConPTY consumes the child's DECSET mouse/focus negotiation before Termwright's VT observer can prove the active protocol. An opaque child therefore remains fail-closed. Instrumenting selected JavaScript stdout methods is not authoritative: fs.writeSync/native descriptor writes and inherited descendant output bypass that surface. Pointer/focus input is supported only when an explicitly registered provider backed by the application's production input-mode state publishes revision-bound evidence; the driver still rejects provider loss or disagreement with observable VT state. This is an observability limit, not a claim that ConPTY cannot carry the input bytes.
deviations.evidence: packages/conformance/src/suites/driver-generic.test.ts "fails closed when ConPTY hides terminal input modes"; packages/probe-ink/src/terminal-tracker.test.ts "does not treat direct descriptor/native or descendant writes as observed input modes"; packages/probe-ink/src/provider.pty.test.ts positive production-provider and negative opaque-child cases
deviations.removalCondition: The certified backend exposes child input-mode negotiation authoritatively for every writer and descendant, so generic applications no longer need production-parser evidence.
deviations.revalidate: each native PTY or Windows certification change
